title: Weak biduality for ordinary constructible sheaves
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, $r\geq1$, and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z$. Schemes below are Noetherian excellent schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Use pinned potential dualizing complexes for dimension functions [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex], the bounded constructible small etale category $D^b_c$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], and $D_K=R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(-,K)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Write $\eta_M:M\to D_K^2M$ for the transpose of evaluation after symmetry of the tensor factors. For every such $X$, every dimension function, every pinned potential $K$, and every constructible sheaf $M$ in degree zero, $\eta_M$ induces isomorphisms on cohomology in all degrees $a\leq0$. Equivalently, the factorization through ordinary truncation is an isomorphism $$M\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau_{\leq0}D_K^2M.$$ This makes no assertion about $\mathcal H^a(D_K^2M)$ for $a>0$.

proof.text: Write $B(M)=D_K^2M$, and call a degree-zero constructible sheaf weakly reflexive when $H^a(\eta_M)$ is an isomorphism for every $a\leq0$. By [lem-per-potential-dual-constructibility], both dualizations stay bounded constructible. For the coefficient sheaf, $D_K\Lambda_X=K$: the underived functor $\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(\Lambda_X,-)$ is the identity on every complex. Under this identification, the transpose of evaluation $\eta_{\Lambda_X}:\Lambda_X\to R\mathcal Hom(K,K)$ sends a scalar to scalar multiplication. Hence [lem-per-potential-scalar-rigidity] proves weak reflexivity of $\Lambda_X$ for every scheme and potential complex under consideration.

For $0\to A\to E\to C\to0$, [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] supplies a triangle. By [lem-per-relative-bidual-triangles] its bidual is a triangle and $\eta$ is a morphism of triangles. Apply the long exact sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact]. If $C$ is weakly reflexive, then $H^aB(C)=0$ for $a<0$ and $C\cong H^0B(C)$. Consequently $H^aB(A)\to H^aB(E)$ is an isomorphism for $a<0$, and $$0\to H^0B(A)\to H^0B(E)\to H^0B(C)\to H^1B(A)$$ is exact. If $E$ is weakly reflexive, its map to $H^0B(C)$ is the surjection $E\to C$, and the kernel is $A$; thus $A$ is weakly reflexive. Conversely, if $A$ is weakly reflexive, the image of $H^0B(E)\to H^0B(C)$ contains the image of $E\to C$, by naturality and the isomorphism for $C$; it is therefore surjective. The two short exact rows now identify $E$ with $H^0B(E)$, and the negative groups vanish. Thus $E$ is weakly reflexive if and only if $A$ is. Finite direct sums and direct summands preserve weak reflexivity: the additive natural map $\eta$ is block diagonal, so its degreewise kernels and cokernels decompose into those of the summands.

Let $p:Y\to X$ be finite. Its source is Noetherian and excellent: on affine charts its rings are finite modules, hence finite-type algebras over the excellent Noetherian rings of $X$; excellence follows from [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]. The integer $\ell$ remains invertible. A finite morphism is proper [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], hence separated and of finite type, so the identity open immersion followed by $p$ is a compactification, and compact support along it is $Rp_!=p_*$; thus the exceptional pullback of the finite-pullback lemma is the right adjoint of finite direct image used in the comparison. Thus [lem-per-potential-dualizing-finite-pullback] gives the induced dimension function and the pinned potential $K_Y=p^!K_X$. The transcendence degrees in this dimension function are zero because residue extensions of finite morphisms are finite. By [lem-per-potential-dual-constructibility] both duality functors preserve $D^b_c$. All hypotheses of [lem-per-potential-finite-bidual-comparison] hold. That statement identifies $p_*H^a(\eta_N)$ with $H^a(\eta_{p_*N})$ and makes $p_*$ exact and conservative. Hence $N$ is weakly reflexive if and only if $p_*N$ is, for every constructible sheaf $N$ on $Y$. This includes closed immersions; no surjectivity of $p$ is needed.

For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$ with complementary reduced closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$, the coefficient sequence is $$0\to j_!\Lambda_U\to\Lambda_Y\to i_*\Lambda_Z\to0$$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact]. The closed scheme $Z$ is again Noetherian excellent with invertible $\ell$, as in Step 3, and its pinned potential comes from $i^!K_Y$. Step 1 proves weak reflexivity of $\Lambda_Y$ and $\Lambda_Z$; Step 3 proves it for $i_*\Lambda_Z$. The implication from middle and quotient to kernel in Step 2 proves it for $j_!\Lambda_U$. A second application of Step 3 proves it for $p_*j_!\Lambda_U$ for every finite $p:Y\to X$.

First assume $r=1$, so the coefficient ring is the finite field $\mathbf F_\ell$. Apply [lem-per-constructible-finite-open-constant-generation] to $X$. It states that every constructible sheaf is obtained by finitely many extensions, finite direct sums and direct summands from $p_*j_!\mathbf F_\ell$ with $p$ finite and $j$ open in its integral source. Step 4 supplies all those generators, and Step 2 supplies each closure operation. Induction on this finite construction proves weak reflexivity for every constructible $\mathbf F_\ell$-sheaf. The zero sheaf and the empty scheme are covered by the empty sum.

For general $r$, set $k=\mathbf F_\ell$ and $K_1=R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(k_X,K)$. It is a pinned potential complex over $k$ by [lem-per-potential-hom-coefficient-restriction]. By [lem-per-potential-coinduction], after restriction of scalars $D_KN\cong D_{K_1}N$ for every bounded constructible $k$-complex $N$; applying it to $N$ and then to $D_{K_1}N$ gives $D_K^2N\cong D_{K_1}^2N$. The second application is allowed by [lem-per-potential-dual-constructibility]. These comparisons identify the biduality maps: on injective representatives coinduction sends $\phi$ to $\operatorname{ev}_1\circ\phi$; the pairing $N\otimes D_{K_1}N\to K$ is therefore $\operatorname{ev}_1$ composed with evaluation into $K_1$. Transposing this same pairing, after symmetry, is both $\eta_N$ over $\Lambda$ and the image of $\eta_N$ over $k$. This proves the identification without assuming biduality. Step 5 applies to $(X,\delta,K_1)$, so every constructible sheaf killed by $\ell$, regarded as a $\Lambda$-sheaf, is weakly reflexive.

The finite filtration $$0=\ell^rM\subseteq\ell^{r-1}M\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\ell M\subseteq M$$ has constructible terms and quotients by [thm-constructible-serre]: each image is the kernel of the cokernel of scalar multiplication. Every quotient $\ell^aM/\ell^{a+1}M$ is killed by $\ell$, so Step 6 proves it weakly reflexive. Starting from zero and applying the extension implication in Step 2 at each short exact sequence proves that $M$ is weakly reflexive. Only $r$ finite steps are used.

Finally, the ordinary truncation adjunction in [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] factors $\eta_M$, since $M$ lies in $D^{\leq0}$, uniquely as $M\to\tau_{\leq0}B(M)\to B(M)$. By [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], the factor has the same maps on cohomology for $a\leq0$ and both its source and target have zero cohomology above zero. Steps 5–7 make all its cohomology maps isomorphisms, hence it is an isomorphism in the derived category, whose inverted maps are quasi-isomorphisms. This is exactly the asserted truncation statement; positive cohomology of $B(M)$ has not been used.
